correctness.rationale: For 0<alpha<1 the difference-coordinate weight exp(tau|m-n|^alpha) is symmetric submultiplicative and GRS: nth roots along each lattice direction tend to 1. The algebra therefore has exactly the torus of multiplicative characters, including the nonproper diagonal direction. Geometric convolution inverse of delta_0-(t/2)(delta_(1,0)+delta_(0,1)) is the binomial random-walk resolvent. Summing over difference fibers reduces its exact weighted l1 norm to (1+2 sum_{k>=1} exp(tau k^alpha-beta k))/sqrt(1-t²), beta=acosh(1/t). A strictly concave saddle h(x)=tau x^alpha-beta x has r=(alpha tau/beta)^(1/(1-alpha)), H=(1-alpha)tau r^alpha, and curvature sigma^-2=tau alpha(1-alpha)r^(alpha-2). Since sigma→infinity and sigma/r→0, Taylor expansion with controlled tails yields the full Gaussian Laplace equivalent and weak Gaussian limit for |m-n|. beta~sqrt(2(1-t)) gives the exponent constant; the zero fiber is negligible. Independent finite Green-kernel recurrence at t=.61,k=3 agreed with explicit formula to floating accuracy. Finite tests do not establish infinite sum asymptotics.

value.rationale: A concrete, motivated sharp stability witness for inverse-closed Beurling algebras: the character spectrum stays fixed at the torus while the inverse develops explicitly quantified stretched-exponential norm blow-up and a concentrated Gaussian difference displacement. Such a tight localized counterpoint to qualitative GRS spectral invariance is useful even though the filter is simple; the novel contribution asserted is the exact evaluated asymptotic, not a new generic Wiener lemma.
